entries.explanation: Unity, the source point from which all number and multiplicity proceed. In Pythagorean number-mysticism the One is not itself reckoned a number but the principle that generates every number, symbolizing the Cosmic before its division into the many.
Duality, polarity, the first division of the One into opposites—light and dark, positive and negative, active and receptive—whose interplay generates every subsequent form.

Synthesis; the number of body-soul-spirit, of the Tria Prima, and of every trinity by which two opposites resolve into a third, new condition. Held throughout the ancient world as a number of completeness and creative power.
The four elements, the four cardinal points of the Lodge, the four stages of the Magnum Opus—foundation, stability, and the physical world's structure made visible in number.
Man himself, the microcosm, pictured in the five-pointed star with the human figure at its center; also the five objective senses and the five-fold path of Rosicrucian concentration.
Harmony and equilibrium, pictured in the hexagram of two interlaced triangles—one rising, one descending—uniting the above and the below, spirit and matter, in a single balanced figure.

Completion of a natural cycle: the seven classical planets, the seven days, the seven psychic centers of the psychic body, and the Cosmic Keyboard's octaves. Widely held to be the number of spiritual perfection.
Regeneration and infinity, its form the lemniscate turned upright; the number of renewal following the completion of seven, and in Christian and Egyptian symbolism, the number of resurrection.
The triple triad (3×3), traditionally the number of attainment and completion before return to unity at ten; associated with gestation, initiation, and the finishing of a matter.
The Pythagorean number of completeness, the sum of the sacred Tetractys (1+2+3+4=10); the closing of one cycle of number and the seed of the next.
A number of excess and transition, falling beyond the completeness of ten and short of the order of twelve; read as a threshold number, marking imbalance that must resolve into higher order.

Cosmic order made complete: twelve signs of the zodiac, twelve months, twelve tribes, twelve disciples, and, in this fellowship, twelve Steps—a governing structure through which a whole cycle is organized and lived.
Transformation, death, and rebirth; the thirteen lunar cycles of the solar year, exceeding the ordered twelve and traditionally marking the passage into a new order beyond the old.
Reconstitution after dismemberment; in the Osiris myth the god's body is cut into fourteen pieces and gathered again, making fourteen a number of the work of restoring what has been scattered.
Amplification and temptation; in esoteric number-symbolism a number historically associated with material bondage that must be mastered rather than yielded to.
Sudden collapse and rebuilding; the number of structures thrown down so that a truer foundation can be laid, a destruction that precedes and enables renewal.
Hope and regeneration following collapse; in esoteric number-symbolism the star that appears after the tower falls, associated with guidance and quiet renewal.
The subconscious and its illusions; the number of the reflected, uncertain light that must be passed through before the clarity of full illumination is reached.
Illumination; the clear, undivided light following the passage through subconscious uncertainty, long read as a number of vitality, joy, and open understanding.
Judgment and awakening; a reckoning number, associated with the call to rise, take account, and answer for the cycle just completed.
Completion and cosmic consciousness; the number of a finished cycle carried to its highest expression, integrating all that came before into a single realized whole.
The master-builder number; the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew alphabet and the twenty-two paths of the Tree of Life, by which the abstract is given structure and built into concrete form.
Governance and completeness in time; the twenty-four hours of the day and, in sacred literature, the twenty-four elders who stand in the presence of the throne.
The lunar month and the feminine cycle; a number of completed rhythm, marking one full turning of the Moon through all its phases.
Maturity; the age of full readiness for a life's work in a number of ancient traditions, marking the close of preparation and the opening of active service.

Mastery through compassion; associated with the vertebrae of the human spine, the years of a completed teaching life, and the highest degrees of initiatic orders, where mastery is expressed as service to others.
Hidden righteousness; in Kabbalistic tradition the number of the concealed just persons for whose sake the world is sustained.
Trial and purification; the number of testing throughout scripture and myth—forty days, forty years—the fixed period a matter must be carried before it is permitted to come to completion.
Moral accounting; the forty-two assessor-gods before whom the Egyptian dead made the Negative Confession at the weighing of the heart, one for each region and each law of Maat.
Completion squared (7×7); the number of days of the between-state in several traditions, and of the counting from one great feast to the next—a full cycle of cycles.
Liberation and jubilee; the number of release that follows forty-nine, in which bondage is set aside and a new order of freedom begins.
Time itself made countable; the base of the ancient Babylonian number system, still preserved in the sixty minutes and sixty seconds by which the Cosmic's motion is measured.
The full field of change; the sixty-four hexagrams of the I Ching, mapping every configuration through which a situation may pass, eight multiplied by itself.
The divine names; seventy-two is one-fifth of the 360 degrees of the zodiac circle and, in Kabbalistic tradition, the number of letter-combinations forming the seventy-two-fold Name of God.
Completion of completion (9×9); the number of chapters of the Tao Te Ching, read as the fullness of a teaching carried through every stage of its unfolding.
The threshold before wholeness; associated in several traditions with the many attributes or names by which the single Divine nature is described, one short of the round hundred.
Totality expressed in decimal form; the Decad multiplied by itself, a number of completeness so standard it becomes the measure—percent, “per hundred”—by which every other completeness is judged.

Cosmic completeness; twelve times nine, and the count kept on a mala or rosary in Hindu and Buddhist practice for a single round of recitation. Ancient astronomers noted it as roughly the number of solar diameters between the Sun and the Earth; it recurs, more as a converging symbol of the individual soul's relation to the whole Cosmic than as a literal measurement, throughout Eastern and Western esoteric number-lore alike. 108 is also the top angle (in degrees) of the golden triangle (hosting the eye).108:  1 for the all or the unity 0 for the neant and 8 is the infinity symbol upwards.

The two qualities or elemental natures that compose the life essence in our bodies. The A element is the immaterial, invisible, Divine essence; B, the material, earthly, chemical element resulting from what we eat and drink, and from the magnetic and other forces we receive from contact with the earth.

Those given to a person at a distance, whether it be a few feet or many miles. In absent treatments we make ourselves channels through which metaphysical forces may be directed so that harmonium may be restored in another person without immediate contact with him.

Certain processes go on inside our bodies which we do not control. They continue whether we think of them or not. These are involuntary actions, such as those of the heart, stomach, and lungs. Voluntary actions are those of which we are conscious, such as speaking—those for which conscious effort is produced.

The phenomenon or manifestation of the vibrations of Spirit. It is that which involves action, and is the law and order of vibrations. Reality is the law and order of consciousness. It represents the individual appreciation of actualities or manifested vibration. Reality is the product of the individual reception and assimilation of vibrations. Actualities cannot become realities to man until he realizes them. Realization can be affected only by interpretation.

Mystically, one who has attained illumination and a mastery in applying his knowledge of Cosmic laws and principles to the affairs of life. He has a mastery of the knowledge and application of spiritual or Cosmic laws—the finally and completely enlightened personality.

The Maya god of death, ruling with the other lords of Xibalba over the realm of the dead, typically pictured as a skeletal or bloated corpse-figure and associated with decay, night, and the owl as his messenger.

The indelible, eternal records of all events and knowledge which are an integral part of Cosmic Consciousness, the Divine mind. They contain all things past, present, and future. They are not material, written accounts, but the Divine consciousness of past and future events. Consulting the Akashic Records means attuning with Cosmic Consciousness.

The pharaoh (reigned circa 1353-1336 B.C.) who abandoned Egypt's traditional pantheon in favor of near-exclusive devotion to the Aten, the disc of the sun, in what is often called history's first experiment with monotheism — though, in practice, closer to henotheism, the elevation of one god without fully denying the others. He moved the capital to a new city built for the new cult, which was abandoned and its reforms reversed within a few years of his death.

The second stage of the Magnum Opus, following the nigredo—a washing away of the impurities exposed by the blackening, bringing clarity and light back to the purified matter. It is read as the stage of purification proper: the reflective, lunar work of cleansing the self once the old form has been dissolved, in preparation for the stages of illumination still to come.

The ancient art and philosophy, both practical and spiritual, concerned with the transmutation of base substances into nobler ones—commonly pictured as turning lead into gold, but understood by its adepts as an allegory for the purification of the soul. Physical alchemy and spiritual alchemy were held to proceed by the same laws: as the metal is refined by fire, so is the self refined by ordeal.

The name of a former Master of the Great White Brotherhood, who gave jurisdiction over the establishment of mystical centers on the North American Continent during the fifteenth century, and after whom the first Temple in this country was named in 1603. His personality still affects much of the work in this country.

The classic distillation vessel of the alchemist's laboratory: a gourd-shaped body topped by a beaked cap that channels rising vapor into a receiving flask. As a symbol, the alembic is the container in which raw experience is heated, vaporized, and returned in purer form—the vessel of transformation itself.

A symbolic story or drama in which the characters and the story represent ideas, emotions, situations, etc., other than their literal nature and meaning. In Rosicrucian allegories, this symbolic meaning is philosophic and mystical. A ritual drama is an allegory based on ritual or initiatic rites and may constitute in itself a ritual or initiation.

In the East of the Lodge is situated the Altar of the Master, who represents the Greater Light and is, in fact, the Lesser Light in all Lodge convocations, except when the “Vestal Light may more symbolically represent the rising of the Greater Light in all its glory.” Sacred and Holy shall the Altar be, that from its bosom may come intellectual and spiritual illumination. From the Altar come forth “Life, Light, and Love.”

A contraction of the old mystical word Aumen. Its origin is in the Sanskrit Aum and Om. It is a Hebrew word introduced into Egyptian mystic rites to express the hidden and invisible God, or an inspired representative of God. The effect of the word in conjunction with proper breathing is to fix or stabilize certain vibrations previously aroused in the surrounding ether, and to bring about a Cosmic manifestation.
If you petition for special help and your petition is answered, you are obliged, by the Law of AMRA, to make compensation by passing along to others some portion of the blessing you have received.

The understanding, foundational to shamanic cultures worldwide and among the oldest forms of human belief, that spirit inhabits not only people and animals but plants, rivers, mountains, and weather—that the world is not inert matter but a community of persons, most of them not human.

A geared bronze device, recovered from a Roman-era shipwreck off the Greek island of Antikythera and dated to roughly the late second century B.C., now understood to be the oldest known analog computer. Its more than thirty interlocking gears tracked the calendar, predicted solar and lunar eclipses years in advance, and modeled the movements of the sun, moon, and planets — a level of mechanical sophistication not matched again in the historical record for well over a thousand years.

A mountain spirit or lord, one of the most immediate and locally worshipped classes of being in Andean religion — each significant peak its own Apu, guardian of the communities and herds within sight of it, consulted and thanked directly rather than through any more distant, universal deity.

The position of the sun on the vernal equinox moves through the path of the zodiac eastward at the rate of a sign in about 2200 years. This period is referred to astrologically as an Age. Due to this precession, the spring equinox does not begin in Aries as it once did, but in Pisces. When it crosses into the sign Aquarius, the Aquarian Age will have begun.

Exchanging places, persons, and power. You assume you have exchanged places with the other person, assuming the other’s personality. In Divine Assumption, you assume you are exchanging your limited self-consciousness for the consciousness of God.

The alchemist's furnace, built to hold a slow, even heat for weeks or months without tending—sometimes called the “House of the Chick” for its likeness to an incubator. It stands for the sustained, unglamorous discipline beneath every real transformation: not a single dramatic fire, but a steady one, kept alight far longer than any one sitting requires.

A legendary lost continent and civilization, described by Plato and taken up by later esoteric tradition as the common root of the Egyptian and Grecian mystery schools. Some Rosicrucian teachers hold that the ancient Teaching—later expressed through Egypt, Greece, and successive mystical orders—first took form on Atlantis before its destruction, making it, in this symbolic reading, less a place on a map than the mythic point of origin for humanity's inherited wisdom.

The innermost self or soul, held in the principal Upanishadic teaching to be identical in nature with Brahman itself — “Atman is Brahman” — so that the deepest truth of any individual is not a separate, private self but the one universal reality, temporarily appearing as many.

During its temporary residence in the human body, the soul essence keeps in touch or attunement with the great Divine source from which the soul came and to which it returns. All soul-personalities on this earth plane and on the Cosmic plane are in constant attunement. It is because man’s soul-personality is attuned with all other soul-personalities that thought vibrations operate at great distances. By attuning ourselves to the Divine mind we can receive the laws, rules, and facts of knowledge which we can depend upon as being truthful.

An admixture of positive and negative vibrations. The negative vibrations are of the spirit energy of the atoms which compose the substance of our bodies. The positive source of the aura is the Vital Life Force taken into our bodies with each breath. The aura is visible under many conditions and has been photographed and will affect certain instruments. The stronger and healthier the physical body, the more deeply we breathe fresh air, the more magnetic will the aura be. Our auras are not constant. Changes in environment, health, and thinking may change the colors. Just as every living thing has an aura, so do inanimate bodies. In addition, such bodies acquire the magnetic influence of the human aura of those in whose possession they have been. They retain in their own nature the radiations of the human aura.

Divine inspiration; in Welsh, literally “flowing spirit.” In Druidic and bardic tradition, awen is the creative breath that moves through poets, seers, and prophets, often symbolized by three rays of light radiating from a single point.

The cosmic center or “world navel” that connects the Lower, Middle, and Upper Worlds—commonly pictured as a great tree, mountain, or pillar whose roots, trunk, and branches join the three realms into a single, traversable structure.

An Andean principle, central to many indigenous cosmologies, holding that giving and receiving must be kept in sacred balance between people, and between people and the natural and spirit worlds—summarized as “today for you, tomorrow for me.” Nothing is received without an obligation, freely honored, to give something back.

A name for the universal solvent or living spirit the alchemists sought, formed from the first and last letters of several alphabets—A and Z, alpha and omega, aleph and tau—to mark it as the beginning and end of the Work at once. Azoth stands for the single creative principle running through every stage of transformation, present at both its start and its completion.

In Tibetan Buddhism, an intermediate or in-between state — most often the interval between death and the next rebirth, but also applied to the gaps of dream, meditation, and the moment of dying itself. Traditionally reckoned at up to forty-nine days, the bardo is a period in which the consciousness, freed from the body, encounters a sequence of visions and choices that shape the nature of the rebirth to follow.

entries.word: Bardo Thodol (Tibetan Book of the Dead)
entries.explanation: A text of instructions read aloud to, or for, a dying or newly dead person, guiding their consciousness through the bardo toward a favorable rebirth or, ideally, liberation from rebirth altogether. Its Tibetan title translates as “Liberation through Hearing in the Intermediate State”; the now-familiar English title was given by its early twentieth-century translator, in deliberate echo of the Egyptian Book of the Dead.

From the mystical point of view, belief implies lack of knowledge. A mystic should have no beliefs, but knowledge, or frankly admit that he does not know. We either know or do not know; and what we know, we must realize that we do, so that we can demonstrate it.

The spring fire festival marking the opening of summer's half of the year, celebrated with bonfires, the greening of the land, and rites of fertility and union — the seasonal counterpart and opposite pole to Samhain.

Occurs, mystically, when the animal body takes its first Breath of Life. Then the body becomes a conscious being. Birth is the opposite phase of the passing of the Breath and consciousness which is falsely called death.

The Buryat and wider Mongolic word for a shaman (from the older Mongol boge), serving the community as healer, diviner, and intermediary with the spirit world through trance and drumming, in a role structurally close to the noaidi of the Sami or the shaman of Tungusic tradition.

A collection of spells, prayers, and instructions, written on papyrus and placed with the dead, meant to guide the soul safely through the dangers of the underworld to the judgment hall of Osiris and beyond. Its most famous section, the Negative Confession, is spoken by the deceased before the scales of Maat at the weighing of the heart.

The merging of the objective and subjective processes into the subconscious. This state can be induced through concentration, or by drugs, fever, injury, fright, or strain. It occurs naturally on going to sleep or awakening. It may be externally induced, but not without cooperation of the self. Often the first stage of transition is a borderline state. In a borderline state it is possible for the two phases of the one mind to hold communion and transfer the ideas, impressions, wishes and desires from one to the other. When we are wholly in the subconscious, we are not immediately aware of what the subconscious received, and we must wait until a borderline condition comes and the idea or impression is released from the subconscious to the objective.

The creator within the triad, who brings the universe into being at the start of each cosmic cycle. Despite this role, Brahma is rarely the object of active worship today, temples and devotion having gathered instead around Vishnu and Shiva.

The single, impersonal, absolute reality underlying and pervading the entire universe in Hindu philosophy — without form, without limit, the ground from which all gods, souls, and matter arise and into which all things ultimately return. Every particular deity is understood as one face, turned toward humanity, of this one unbounded ground.

A supremely destructive, divinely sanctioned weapon described in the Mahabharata and other Hindu epics, said to be capable of leveling cities and armies at a single stroke. Its vivid ancient description — a single projectile as bright as ten thousand suns, followed by lingering sickness and destruction across generations — has been popularly compared by some modern writers to a nuclear detonation, a comparison mainstream historians and Indologists regard as anachronistic, reading twentieth-century weapons back into Bronze Age epic poetry rather than evidence of literal ancient nuclear technology.

The physical organ for the objective functioning of the mind. Mind, however, can manifest without the use of the brain. All action of the brain is vibratory. Thinking accelerates and stimulates the vibrations. Sleep slows them down. The brain and mind are two distinctly different things in function. Mind is a manifestation of the soul which functions independently at times from the brain. The brain is the medium by which the objective consciousness functions.
In Rosicrucian teachings this term is used to refer to Nous. It is a combination, so to speak, of both the Vital Life Force and Cosmic Consciousness.

Goddess of poetry, healing, and smithcraft, whose sacred flame at Kildare was tended without interruption for centuries. Her festival, Imbolc, marks late winter's first stirring toward spring, and she was carried with little alteration into Christian tradition as Saint Brigid.

The school or fraternity of the Great White Lodge. Into this invisible Brotherhood of visible members every true student on the Path prepares for admission. There is an assembly of Master minds, some on the Cosmic plane, some on the earth plane, who constitute the Holy Assembly. Under their care, a group of high Initiates are prepared in each incarnation for still higher work in the next. These Imperators, Magi, and Hierophants in various lands, together with the Masters, compose the Holy Assembly of the Great White Lodge. There is no authoritative physical group termed the Great White Lodge.

The first operation of the Magnum Opus: a substance is roasted in an open fire until it is reduced to ash, its moisture and volatile matter burned away. Symbolically, calcination is the burning-off of pride, illusion, and excess self-image—a stripping down to what will not burn.

A long-stemmed ceremonial pipe of the Plains and other Native nations, called by outsiders the “peace pipe” though its own keepers simply call it the sacred pipe. Smoked to open councils, seal agreements, and accompany prayer, each puff of smoke is understood to carry intention and gratitude upward — an offering made of breath rather than words.

A Cosmic meeting place for all minds of the most highly developed and spiritually advanced members and workers of the Rosicrucian fraternity. It is the focal point of Cosmic radiations and thought waves from which radiate vibrations of health, peace, happiness, and inner awakening. The Cathedral is a concentration of the spiritual selves of all those members who seek Cosmic attunement. It is, abstractly, a plane of consciousness where there are assembled the many minds who have similar impersonal ideals.

A body of spherical or other shape having a wall with negative polarity and a nucleus of positive polarity. The cell is the fundamental form of all creation. Every living cell floating in a liquid is connected with every other cell in that liquid by a force which pervades them all. Man’s relation to the universe is identical to this. We have no distinct individuality so far as our beings are concerned. We are all united in the universe as the cells are united in a mass of flesh, bone, or blood. The sun is a cell with a positive polarity. The earth is also a magnetic cell with a negative polarity. The nucleus is the focal point, the center of action, the heart of any creation possessing, latent within itself, all the potentialities of development in connection with a cell. On the earth plane the nucleus of the cell is positive in polarity and the rest negative. On the immaterial plane the elements are in reverse order. The nucleus has within itself all the characteristics of former unions in previous generations, and in each successive manifestation blends in the additional characteristics of the present union, thereby establishing the conditions and qualities of heredity.

The horned or antlered god of the Celts, attested by name only once, on the first-century Pillar of the Boatmen, and known otherwise through images pairing him with animals, a torc, and a horned serpent. As Lord of the Animals and a liminal deity ruling the Otherworld, he opens the gate between life and death and is associated with wild nature, healing, and abundance — a widely recognized figure in modern Celtic paganism.

One of the body's subtle energy centers, most often enumerated as seven and arranged along the spine from base to crown, through which vital and spiritual energy is understood to flow and by which its balance or blockage is read.

The conscious code of thought, practice, emotion, and act, which the school of personality has established for the person, and which the traits of personality are emulating as an ideal. The code, the ideal, toward which progress is being made may be consciously realized, the acts tending toward that ideal may be unconsciously committed.

A Tibetan Buddhist practice, meaning “to cut through,” in which the practitioner visualizes offering their own body, dismembered, as a feast to hungry spirits and demons, deliberately confronting fear and the illusion of a fixed, defended self in order to cut through attachment to it.

The Christian delineation of the highest form of consciousness attainable. The moral values, powers, and insight had by Christ are attributed to his all-embracing consciousness, the result of his attunement with the Divine of his own nature. The term has no significance different from Cosmic Consciousness. The non-Christian mystic prefers the latter term because this universal or Cosmic Consciousness has been had by other illuminated personages and should have no personal designation.

The third stage of the Magnum Opus, in which the dawning of an inner, solar light begins to replace the reflected, lunar light of the albedo. Where the whitening stage purifies by washing, the yellowing stage illuminates from within—the alchemist's own understanding, rather than a borrowed clarity, beginning to shine.

The operation in which the purified, fermented matter is fused with the sublimated spirit released in distillation, binding what was volatile into a fixed, stable, and permanent form. It is the final act of the Work: not further refinement, but the settling of everything refined into one lasting substance.

The word Colombe means dove. In earlier Rosicrucian Temples there were one or more Vestal Virgins who not only kept the important symbolical and holy fire in the Vestal Stand ever burning, but who also served in the ritualistic work and mystical exercises as a symbol of fire, light, life, and love, and the dove of consciousness. The Colombe also represents the conscience of each Frater and Soror of the Lodge.

A mental and physical state in which the whole objective attention is focused on one point, place, condition, or principle. Perfect concentration results in complete inactivity of four of the five objective faculties at one time. We can be conscious of only one objective impression at one time. All else is rapid alternation. Concentration is not merely the focalization of attention. The real art of concentration consists in turning the objective thoughts inward until they become fixed ideas of the Inner Self. The Inner Self becomes possessed with the thought or idea, and lives it, senses it, seeing and feeling it with all the living vitality that a thing alive could possibly have. Concentration is not will power. Passivity is necessary to concentration and precludes the use of energized will power.

The “chemical wedding”—the operation in which two opposed principles, commonly pictured as King and Queen, Sun and Moon, Sulphur and Mercury, are joined into a single new substance. Conjunction stands for the marriage of soul and spirit, or of any two long-separated parts of the self, from which a third, integrated nature is born.

The “still, small voice” of the Master within; the Cosmic mind with its inspiration and urge; the mind of the psychic self, knowing all truth, all law, all principles, ever constructive in desire, dependable, “ever present when the tempter tempts.”

An attribute of the soul. It is the mental aspect of life which includes sensation, realization, and reasoning of which the active principles are imagination, aspiration, and inspiration. It is the center of man’s life, poised between two worlds, and naturally open to both. One of the functions of consciousness is the response to its environment or surroundings. Another is the response which the animate thing has to its own innate actions or being. The Divine Consciousness in man has its own faculties for the perception of truth and its own domain of functioning. This spiritual consciousness is the inner self. The physical consciousness can become acquainted only with things of a material nature. Consciousness, life force, and mind are related and come into and go out of the body together.

The technique whereby the fingers are placed upon the patient’s back close to the spine is called the system of “Rosicrucian contact treatment.” This is because the one who is giving the treatment has to be in actual physical contact with the patient.

A method distilled by anthropologist Michael Harner, founder of the Foundation for Shamanic Studies, from the universal and near-universal features he found common to shamanic traditions on every inhabited continent, once each culture's particular gods, costumes, and cosmology are set aside. What remains is a portable technique: reaching the shamanic state of consciousness—most often through sustained, monotonous drumming at roughly four to seven beats a second, the drum acting as the shaman's horse—in order to journey to the Lower, Middle, or Upper World, meet one's power animal or helping spirits, and bring back healing, guidance, or a retrieved part of the soul. Core shamanism is deliberately not a religion or a culture of its own; it is offered as a set of practices that a person from any background can learn and then, if they choose, root back into a specific tradition's fuller cosmology.

Used both as a noun and adjective to mean the Universe as a harmonious relation of all natural and spiritual laws. It is the Divine, infinite intelligence of the Supreme Being permeating everything. It is not a place, but a state, or condition of order and regulation. The Cosmic is the totality of laws and the phenomena which manifests in man and nature—the forces, energies, and powers which account for the finite and infinite worlds. It is therefore a unity; the particulars which man experiences are but expressions.

That consciousness, radiating from God, which pervades all space, and hence all things, having vitality, mind, constructive power, Divine Intelligence. Into this consciousness is projected the psychic consciousness of all Masters, and all adepts may attune with it. It is the unity of all, past, present, and future. The universal force exhibits the desire to be; therefore, it manifests intelligence. That which has mind and intelligence has consciousness, so the Cosmic force has a Cosmic consciousness which is the inherent sensitivity of this universal creative force by which it at all times opposes any possible depreciation of its own nature. Consequently, it extends its Cosmic consciousness into all things which it forms or which are formed of it. It accompanies the universal Cosmic energy as an attribute into every living cell where it manifests with the vibratory force. Man must attune with the Cosmic consciousness, be in accord with it, be in sympathy with its oneness.

An association of officers, staff, and certain high-degree Rosicrucian members who use the principles of the Order’s teachings to assist other individuals. Absent treatments are given for conditions of health, and other problems of a personal nature whenever they are brought to the attention of the Council.
The looped cross, a tau or T cross with a loop at the top. It is of ancient Egyptian origin and was referred to as the Ankh or key of life. It was a symbol of life and immortality.

A period of time, evolution, process, method, or manifestation. The cycle of human life is divided into seven-year cycles of the growth and development of the mind and body. The evolution of the universe, and of man from a primitive being can be divided into cycles. The twenty-four hours of the day are divisible into planetary cycles. There is a cycle of existence or incarnation for each being, according to which each human being is reborn on the earth plane on an average of every 144 years.

A necessary element in the cycle of life. Death and birth are synonymous in this sense, for death is birth into another plane, while birth is likewise a transition. Both constitute the Great Experience, a form of Initiation affording an opportunity for greater advancement. There is no “death” either material or spiritual. Matter is indestructible; the soul essence is immortal. Hence neither body nor soul ever dies. In death the soul has departed from one state of existence to another. The soul continues but manifests differently. The consciousness has crossed a threshold from the chamber of life into the Cosmic and has been initiated into a higher Degree.

One's right conduct, duty, and place within the cosmic and social order — the law by which each being, action, and stage of life is aligned with the universal order that sustains existence. To live according to one's dharma is to act in harmony with reality itself.

The outer manifestation of something wrong on the inside. Treating the last stage of a wrong condition is not the way to regain health and prevent recurrence of the trouble. Disease is a disturbance of the harmonious constructive process of the living cells. The logical procedure is to help nature by not interfering, and by ending the cause of the disturbance when it is known. Giving the blood, nerves, and general system what is lacking is the next essential. Hence the various schools of therapeutics may assist in the restoration of health through assisting nature. Disease cannot exist in any area of the body where the negative and positive polarities of the cells are evenly balanced. Disease, or mental or nervous disorder may result from a lack of harmony between the outer and inner man, or from an unbalanced relation of the A and B elements.

An initiatory vision, often unsought, in which the future shaman experiences their own body being taken apart by spirits and reassembled anew. The old, untransformed self is broken down completely so that a stronger, spirit-endowed self can be built in its place.

The operation, paired with Coagulation as one of alchemy's two great directions (“solve et coagula”), in which a fixed substance is dissolved back into liquid so its hidden impurities can be released. Dissolution is the loosening of what has hardened—old certainties, old form—so it can be worked again.

The operation of boiling a liquid to vapor and condensing it again, used to separate a substance's finer essence from its coarser residue. As a symbol, distillation is the repeated refining of experience: rising above the immediate condition of a thing to draw off what is essential in it, then returning changed.

entries.word: Divine Mind (Universal Mind or Cosmic Mind)
entries.explanation: The consciousness of God which pervades all. It is not only the mind of God but also the consciousness and mind of all living beings on the earth plane. These are so united as to be a consensus of mind and thought, in which every inspiration, idea, and expression of universal importance is registered and may be contacted through proper attunement with this Universal Mind. The Supreme Mind is not a collection of individual intelligences. No sum of things alone could equal the Universal Mind, because it is also potential with that which is as yet without discernible nature or form. The Universal Mind as an Intelligence, permeates every cell of our being, and is accessible as an infinite wisdom. However, the Cosmic Mind does not contain within it all the particular details of human knowledge and experience, but is an exalted form of evaluation.

The priestly and learned class of the ancient Celts: philosophers, judges, healers, astronomers, and keepers of oral lore, who committed nothing of their own teaching to writing, so that nearly everything known of them comes down through Greek and Roman observers and later medieval Irish and Welsh literature.

Modern spiritual paths, revived from the eighteenth century onward, that draw on what survives of the old Druidic tradition together with reconstructed and reimagined practice. Contemporary Druidry emphasizes reverence for nature, the turning of the seasonal Wheel of the Year, and the cultivation of Awen, or inspiration.

The oldest runic alphabet, of twenty-four characters, in use among Germanic peoples from roughly the second to the eighth century A.D. and named, like the Latin “alphabet,” for the sound-values of its first six letters: F, U, Th, A, R, K.

Chemistry refers to the 144 elements composing all material creation. Of these, more than 100 are known to man. Fire, earth, air, and water are not elements. They are combinations of elements. They are considered as the four principals, because they are the first four principal manifestations of the elements. In Rosicrucian terminology the term is used to express the three forms into which Nous organizes to compose or manifest matter: electrons, atoms, and molecules. Divinities is a term expressing the first three manifested forms of the elements: solids, liquids, and gases.

The alchemical preparation, closely identified with the philosopher's stone, held to heal all sickness and indefinitely prolong life. Understood spiritually rather than literally, the Elixir stands for the renewed vitality that follows a completed inner transformation—life restored, not merely extended.

A short, cryptic Hermetic text attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, first attested in early Arabic sources and carried into Western alchemy through a twelfth-century Latin translation. Its best-known line—“That which is above is like to that which is below, and that which is below is like to that which is above”—states the principle of correspondence: microcosm and macrocosm mirror each other, and the pattern of the greater world repeats in the lesser. Alchemists read it as an instruction for the Great Work; mystics read it as a description of man's own nature reflecting the Cosmic.

A plant, fungus, or substance used deliberately within a ceremonial or shamanic context to occasion a direct experience of the sacred—literally, to “generate the divine within.” Distinguished by intention and setting from recreational use of the same substances.

Refers to that which is indwelling, innate, secret, or private. Esoteric knowledge may refer to Cosmic enlightenment or intuitive impressions as contrasted with objective experience. The secret wisdom imparted to the initiate is esoteric. The antonym of esoteric is exoteric, the outer aspect.

The progressive growth and perfecting of all that is manifest or in the conception of the Cosmic Mind. Devolution or disintegration is a part of evolution. Evolution is the fundamental law of nature, and every element in nature is tending toward perfection and becoming higher in its rate of vibrations and more evolved in its manifestations. Evolution begins when the initial impulse of a new or higher order or purpose is manifested. Devolution begins when the highest form or expression of evolution is completed.

A healing technique in which the shaman locates and removes intrusive, non-organic energy—commonly pictured as a foreign object lodged in the body—that is understood to be causing illness or distress, restoring the patient's own energy to its proper place.

The All-seeing Eye depicts the all-inclusive vision and consciousness of God from which nothing is excluded. It appears in most Rosicrucian lodges and chapters throughout the world on the Master’s lectern in the “East.”
The pineal gland is a transformer of the Cosmic consciousness into rates of vibration which are discernible by our objective minds. This is the Third Eye, the true eye of the soul.

Reliance upon the implied quality of things and conditions. It should only arise from circumstances of strong probability. Such justified faith should be but a temporary measure to be replaced with knowledge.

The operation in which a substance is seeded with a small living portion of itself and left to work in the dark, producing new life and releasing spirit from matter—as yeast raises dough, or grape becomes wine. Fermentation is the quiet, unseen stage in which something already begun continues to transform on its own.

The Aztec cosmological account of five successive worlds, or “suns,” each created and then destroyed — by jaguars, by hurricane, by fire, by flood, and, in the present and fifth age, by an earthquake yet to come — with humanity re-created anew at the start of each. The current, Fifth Sun is held to be sustained only by continued ritual devotion.

We are asked to form a lodge when the Master enters the Temple and again when he leaves to signify our respect for the office of the Master as the representative of the Order and the Cosmic, symbolic of the Greater Light. Formation of the lodge indicates our readiness to receive the light and instruction which the Master is the means of disseminating.

East, South, West, and North, each honored in turn in ceremony as holding its own power, color, and teaching, with the center — where the person standing in prayer or ceremony is located — sometimes counted as a fifth direction binding the other four together.

The vibratory nature of an object by which it is realized by one of our senses to be a specific object. It signifies to our consciousness what kind of object or physical phenomenon it is. The fourth dimension is the rate of electronic vibration. All qualities and attributes manifested by all material things result from this rate. Without the fourth dimension, there could not be the other three. From the Rosicrucian concept, the fourth dimension should probably be the first.

The Rosicrucian funeral service is a ceremony of celebration in its spirit, at which time those assembled around the body of the Frater or Soror take part in a ritual significant of the passing through a Higher Initiation of the one who is no longer limited by the work of the Order in its material form on this plane.

In Greek mythology, the primordial goddess and personification of the Earth itself, born directly out of Chaos at the beginning of the world and the mother, by various unions, of the sky and sea and of the Titans who preceded the Olympian gods. Gaia is invoked in modern usage, following the scientific Gaia hypothesis, as a name for the Earth understood as a single, self-regulating, living system — an ancient goddess and a contemporary systems-model converging on the same image of a world that is not inert matter but one interdependent living whole.
The elephant-headed god of beginnings, wisdom, and the removal of obstacles, traditionally invoked at the start of any undertaking, journey, or ceremony before any other deity is addressed.

The frame drum of the noaidi, its skin painted with figures mapping the upper, middle, and lower worlds and the beings that inhabit them. Struck to induce trance, the drum's surface also served as a kind of divinatory map: small objects placed on the skin would move toward particular symbols as it was beaten, and the noaidi read the resulting pattern.

There is but one God, everliving, ever-present, without limiting attributes or definite form of manifestation—it is the God of our Hearts. God is wholly a subjective experience and thus a personal interpretation. The concept of God reflects the intelligence, education, religious, and social background of the individual. For these reasons it is impossible to create a uniform conception of God acceptable to all men alike.

A face wreathed or composed of leaves, carved into churches and buildings across Europe for centuries, read in modern Celtic-influenced traditions as the spirit of vegetation and the forest. He is paired with rule over summer's half of the year, opposite a Lord of Winter, and honored especially at Beltane.

Your conscience, your inner self, the sentinel of the subconscious mind, acting as your guide and protector. The Guardian also stands at the Threshold of the Cosmic, of the Unseen, and is at the threshold of every soul, of every chamber of privacy, of every mind.

The pattern formed in the subconscious mind through repetition, or by purposely deciding that a thing shall be done over and over again. We order the subconscious mind to do the thing, and it does it. Habit is an unconscious law of the subconscious mind, a law which has become unconscious to the objective mind.

Within the individual includes health, rhythm, coordination of action in all parts, plus the properly balanced relationship between the psychic and objective functionings. Applied to the relationship between humans, harmony is unity of thought, agreement of purpose, the direct communion or kinship of souls. In the relationship of the Cosmic to the human soul, it means that state of ecstasy where the human becomes conscious of the attunement of the natural forces of his being with the Absolute, or the source from which they emanate.

The ancestral homeland from which, in Maori and wider Polynesian tradition, the first voyagers set out and to which the spirits of the dead return after death. Hawaiki is held to be both a real, once-inhabited place remembered in migration traditions, and a spiritual origin-point and final destination, not fixed to any single map coordinate.

The Rosicrucian system of healing does not deny the good that can be done by medicine, surgery, or other established systems of therapeutics. It is based on the fact that the sympathetic nervous system carries and distributes to all parts of the body an intangible energy that vitalizes organs and cells of the body. It takes into consideration primarily the psychic side of man and the psychic cause and nature of disease and pain.

Any compassionate, non-ordinary-reality being—animal, ancestor, plant, or teacher—that a practitioner comes to know through repeated journeying and that offers guidance, protection, or healing power in return for right relationship.

Rosicrucian records tell us that there actually was such a character as Hermes or Thoth. He was not a god, but a sage born in Thebes in 1399 B.C. He received the appellation “Thrice Illustrious” (Trismegistus) because he participated in the organization of the great mystery school, had the experience of seeing the illustrious Amenhotep IV initiated as a Grand Master, and the honor of assisting in the initiation of the successor to Amenhotep IV. The best known work attributed to Hermes is the Pymander, or the Shepherd of Men.

Seven universal laws attributed to the Hermetic tradition and popularized in the early twentieth century as the foundation of The Kybalion: Mentalism (the All is Mind), Correspondence (as above, so below), Vibration (nothing rests, everything moves), Polarity (opposites are identical in nature, differing only in degree), Rhythm (everything flows, out and in), Cause and Effect (every cause has its effect, every effect its cause), and Gender (gender is in everything, and nothing is created without it). Together they describe the Cosmic as a single, lawful, and knowable order.

Hunahpu and Xbalanque, the central protagonists of the Popol Vuh, who descend into Xibalba to avenge their father, defeat the death lords through cleverness rather than force at every trial set for them, and are transformed at the story's end into the sun and the moon.

The Celestial Hierarchy consisted of a group or assembly of enlightened personalities, not resident in physical bodies, who, as a part of the great Cosmic Mind, were arranged according to their rank of development and enlightenment. The Hierarchy consists of nine spiritual orders, each of three ranks or degrees of development. These enlightened beings become mediators for man; man communes with them, and thus becomes the recipient of an influx of knowledge.

The falcon-headed sky god, son of Isis and Osiris, whose left eye was torn out and restored in his long conflict with his uncle Seth over the throne of Egypt. The restored Eye of Horus (the wedjat) became one of Egypt's most enduring symbols of healing, protection, and wholeness, and each reigning pharaoh was held to be Horus's living embodiment on earth.

The Aztec god of the sun and of war, patron deity of the Mexica people and their capital, Tenochtitlan, said to be born fully armed each dawn to fight off his sister the moon and his siblings the stars in order to win the sun's daily passage across the sky.

A condition induced either by use of drugs or by mental processes. Sleep need not result, nor is it an indication that the person is under control mentally or physically. In mental induction, cooperation on the part of the subject is essential. Use of hypnotism should be limited to physicians or to scientists who have made a careful study of its laws and principles and who have the highest ethical and scientific reasons for inducing the state. Psychically, it is a state where the objective mind is at least four-fifths passive and the subconscious mind is proportionately active.

The Inca god of weather, thunder, and lightning, pictured as a warrior in the sky whose sling-stone strikes cause thunder and whose slingshot throws lightning; also petitioned, alongside Pachamama, for rain in a landscape where irrigation could mean the difference between harvest and famine.

Enlightened ones, those who have received illumination or Cosmic consciousness. The Illuminati were well established in Southern France and were one and the same as the Rosicrucians. In 1776 Adam Weishaupt established a sect called the Illuminati which had no connection with the older movement, and which concerned itself greatly with politics and came into bad repute.

Refers to enlightenment of the mind. It means not only intellectual but intuitive knowledge imparted directly to the individual from transcendental sources such as the Cosmic. As a result of gradual awakening of various centers of psychic comprehension, there results an awakening of the whole psychic consciousness, and then comes the great influx of illumination. Rosicrucians distinguish illumination from knowledge. The former is apperception or clear understanding, a mere accumulation of ideas gained from experience.

Imaging is visualizing images, making mental pictures of them. Imagining is creating things by bringing together unrelated elements and building them into something concrete and definite in your mind. Imagination includes imaging, but imaging or visualization need not be a form of imagination.

The quality of being inherently present within. Applied to the Divine, the doctrine that God or the Cosmic indwells creation rather than standing apart from it, knowable through nature, self, and the ordinary world. Rosicrucian teaching holds both together: the Cosmic is at once transcendent, beyond full comprehension, and immanent, permeating every cell and every living thing.

A separate, absolute distinctiveness. That which is real in man is an inseparable part of the Great Soul, the Universal Mind. That soul may express itself differently in one body than it would in another body. This difference makes up the personality. It does not give the individuality, which is a material, transient thing. Personality pertains to the Inner Man, the Soul, the Psychic or Divine Being within the physical body. The individuality refers to the transient and mortal, objective side of man.

An experience of the consciousness, the soul, mind, and emotions. It is a simple ceremony which attunes the inner consciousness with the higher principles of the universe, and reveals to the consciousness many laws of God and nature. It is an awakening of the inner consciousness. “Initiation brings into the realm of reason the purpose and into the realm of emotion the spirit of one’s introduction into the mysteries.” The initiate is the candidate for the initiation.

The spiritual consciousness within the physical human body. It has its own immaterial faculties and functionings, and constitutes a separate form from the physical form in which it temporarily resides. This consciousness constitutes man’s real being and is part of the soul or the divine element of man’s existence. The spiritual consciousness of man is different in essence from the material part of man. The two are related, for they are both part of the same Cosmic whole. However, matter and Divine consciousness in man constitute two different realities working in harmonious parallel. The outer self with its material, physical consciousness is limited in the nature and quality of contact it can make. The inner self, the spiritual consciousness, is unlimited and in no way restricted by “time” or “space,” or by the nature and quality of material things.

The Inca sun god, ancestral father of the Inca royal line and the most widely worshipped deity of the Tawantinsuyu, the Inca empire, honored above all at the June solstice festival of Inti Raymi, the “Festival of the Sun,” which marked the Andean new year.

Intuitive knowledge is that knowledge which appears self-evident and which flashes suddenly into the consciousness and about which we entertain no doubt. It is the intelligence of the Cosmic Mind, resident in the subconscious, which periodically enters the objective mind as a complete idea commonly called a hunch. Intuition is an expression of the Cosmic consciousness in man through the attunement which the Inner Self has with the Universal Mind.

Goddess of magic, motherhood, and skilled speech, who reassembled the dismembered body of her husband Osiris after his murder, conceived Horus by him, and through her mastery of ritual words restored Osiris to a new form of life in the underworld. Her cult, among the most enduring and widely traveled of the ancient Mediterranean, carried her worship as far as Rome long after Egypt itself had passed into other hands.

A traditional Sami form of vocalization, sung not primarily about a person, place, or animal but understood as directly evoking or embodying it. Used by the noaidi to summon spirits, induce trance, and heal, and, outside ritual, as an everyday way of holding someone or something in song.

A fierce form of the great goddess, associated with time, death, and the destruction of illusion and ego — typically pictured dark-skinned, garlanded with skulls, tongue extended, standing upon the prone form of Shiva. Terrifying in appearance, she is understood by devotees as a mother who destroys only what must fall away.

The law of compensation and causality. This means that for every cause we institute, an effect follows. For each sorrow or pain we cause another, we shall suffer in like degree and manner when the lesson to be gained will be most impressive. However, the principle does not exact an eye for an eye. It is not retributive, that is, vengeful; rather, its purpose is to teach a lesson and evolve the understanding. The law works two ways; that is, one may have karmic credit due as well as debt. There is collective as well as individual karma.

The substance of the Universal Being or the Cosmic consists of all the forces and energies of which we have knowledge. They compose a Cosmic keyboard. The Cosmic Mind works through a sea of vibratory energy which is one vast spectrum or keyboard. The highest octaves produce what is termed psychic phenomena.

An ornate script descended from Old Khmer, used in central and northern Thailand exclusively for sacred purposes: Buddhist manuscripts, protective diagrams, and the mantras (kata) inscribed in sak yant tattooing. Written in Pali, the liturgical language of Theravada Buddhism, rather than everyday Thai, Khom script marks a text as ritually potent by the simple fact of the alphabet it is written in.

The Rosicrucians hold that one cannot know of a thing except through personal experience. For this reason, a distinction is made between belief and knowledge. The necessary experience may be through objective realization or psychic reality, but there must be the personal realization. It is customary for the mystic to say that he either knows or does not know when speaking of experiences, problems, or facts of life and nature; he accepts nothing on faith, and he has no beliefs.

The feathered-serpent deity of the Maya, associated with wind, learning, and the planet Venus, and closely related to Gukumatz of the K'iche' Maya and to Quetzalcoatl of the Aztecs — one figure appearing, with local variation, across nearly the whole of Mesoamerican religion.

A latent, coiled energy pictured resting at the base of the spine, which spiritual practice may awaken and draw upward through the body's subtle centers to the crown, bringing expanded consciousness as it rises. It is frequently personified as a sleeping serpent goddess.

entries.word: Laozi and the Tao Te Ching
entries.explanation: Laozi (“Old Master”), the semi-legendary sage traditionally credited as the founder of philosophical Taoism and author of the Tao Te Ching, its foundational text of some eighty-one short, paradoxical chapters on the Tao, wu wei, and the wisdom of yielding. Whether Laozi was a single historical person, several authors, or a figure assembled after the fact remains genuinely unresolved by scholarship.

The combination of the vital life force with the manifestations of spirit. The essential characteristics of the live body are activity, voluntary and involuntary, and consciousness. In the human body, every cell possesses and manifests the existence of an energy called spirit, which is found in everything that exists. There is also a form of consciousness in every cell of the animate body that is of a higher rate. This vitality is called life.

The threshold condition—from the Latin limen, threshold—in which a person has left one state or status but has not yet arrived at the next: neither who they were nor who they are becoming. Identified by anthropologist Victor Turner as the volatile, generative middle phase of every rite of passage.

A body of Rosicrucian students united for the purpose of working and studying together under the jurisdiction of the Grand Lodge of AMORC. In the Rosicrucian system, active members of the Grand Lodge receiving monographs and carrying on their studies in home sanctums may further promote the work by organizing lodges, chapters, or pronaoi. A lodge is required to have permanent quarters, conduct at least three convocations a month and maintain a library available to members and the public at least four days a week. Only a lodge is permitted to conduct Temple Degree initiations. A chapter represents at least forty active members and is required to conduct a minimum of two convocations a month. A pronaos is the smallest body that may be organized and must have at least fifteen members. Its status is expected to change as soon as its membership increases to the minimums set for chapters and lodges.

This is the central chamber devoted to the general convocation and formal study of God’s works. It is the “inner” or “middle” chamber, the Soul of the Temple, the first circle within the great circle. Our Lodges represent the surface of the earth with four cardinal points. The East of the Lodge is the first point on the horizon. In the East the new life is begun. It is the place of Divine Illumination and Resurrection. The South is the point where the sun shines in greatest glory, and where the Divine Mind finds fullest spiritual expression. In the West the sun of life closes its journey. It is where the Fratres and Sorores seek peace, rest, and attunement with the Cosmic. The North is the place of “dismal darkness” where the sun sheds not its glorious light. It is the abyss of evil, the valley of death, the realm of darkness, the hours of the night where the Seeker for Light dwells and the Neophyte enters the Lodge in search of more light.

This is a body subordinate to, and deriving its existence and powers from, the Imperator and the Board of Directors composing the Supreme Grand Lodge of AMORC. It is a separate and distinct body from the Supreme Grand Lodge, and with its properly authorized subordinate bodies and members at large, constitutes the membership section of the Order in The Americas, British Commonwealth, France, Switzerland, Sweden, and Africa.

This is the legal, corporate body of the Rosicrucian Order, incorporated under the laws of California as a nonprofit organization. The general administration of the Order is governed by the Board of Directors of the Supreme Grand Lodge of whom the Imperator is President. The general membership of the Order constitutes a separate body under the direction of the Supreme Grand Lodge through the Grand Lodge Executive Committee, composed of the Grand Master, the Grand Secretary, and the Grand Treasurer.

The Maya's non-repeating linear calendar, counting days continuously from a mythic creation date corresponding to 11 August 3114 B.C., used alongside their repeating ritual and solar calendars to fix any date uniquely across vast spans of time rather than only within a repeating cycle.

To the natural Cosmic forces, the physical laws of the universe, man attributes a once uttered Word as their source, which continues to reverberate throughout the universe and which he can no longer, at least in its entirety, apprehend. The Word is conceived as a vibratory, undulating energy in which the basic essence of all things exists. All manifestations owe their existence to the continuous reverberations of the Word throughout the universe. The vibratory nature of each thing thus fits into a gigantic scale or keyboard.

One of the three shamanic worlds, reached by journeying downward—through a tunnel, a cave mouth, a tree's roots, or a spring—into the foundational, life-sustaining depths of the earth, where power animals and ancestral wisdom are most often found.

The Egyptian word for truth. The symbol of Maat was a feather. Cro-Maat means “The Truth shall be,” or “So mote it be.” The Confession to Maat is taken from the confession—contained in the Book of the Dead—spoken in the Chamber of Maat in Egyptian Temples of Initiation.

Presumes there are occult powers in nature which must be invoked by the application of certain agencies. Both natural and supernatural forces, it is believed, can be brought to serve human will. Black magic is the superstitious use of magical rites for malevolent purposes. White magic is the use of these rites for benevolent purposes.

Results from action in the aura that surrounds all matter. It is not a result of the atomic or molecular structure of matter, but rather of an electrical action taking place within the substance or which can be set up in the substance.

The alchemist's complete labor—the sequence of operations by which the prima materia is purified and transformed into the philosopher's stone. Symbolically traced through four stages, the nigredo, albedo, citrinitas, and rubedo, the Great Work stands for the whole arc of self-transformation, from the first blackening dissolution of the old self to the reddened, completed integration of the new.

One of the two great epics of ancient India (with the Ramayana), an immense narrative centered on the succession war between two branches of a royal family, the Pandavas and Kauravas, culminating in the eighteen-day battle of Kurukshetra. Embedded within it is the Bhagavad Gita, the dialogue between the warrior Arjuna and the god Krishna that stands as one of Hinduism's central scriptures.

“The great vehicle”: the broad Buddhist tradition, dominant in East Asia, distinguished by its central ideal of the bodhisattva — one who postpones final liberation to help all other beings toward it first — and by scriptures composed well after the Buddha's death that Theravada does not accept as canonical.

The creator god of Rapa Nui, associated with fertility, seabirds, and the human skull, and chief deity of the Tangata Manu, or Birdman cult, in which rival chiefs' champions competed each year to retrieve the season's first sooty tern egg — the winner's chief holding the sacred title, and something of Makemake's own authority, for the year that followed.

The Inca moon goddess, wife and sister of Inti the sun, who governed the calendar, the months, and women's cycles. Her eclipse was read as an attack by a great serpent or mountain lion upon her, to be driven off with noise and prayer until her light returned.

Spiritual power, authority, and prestige, understood as a real and consequential force that inheres in people, objects, and places, and that can be increased or diminished by one's actions and treatment by others. Mana is inseparable from tapu: right conduct maintains and grows a person's mana, while violation of tapu diminishes it.

A circular diagram, often elaborately symmetrical, representing the universe or a particular deity's realm in miniature, used as a support for meditation and, in some Tibetan traditions, built painstakingly from colored sand and then ceremonially destroyed on completion — a deliberate lesson in impermanence set beside its own careful, geometric order.

The Inner Self. The conscience is this Master’s voice. The soul force brings into our being a Divine Intelligence. The aggregate of this intelligence is our psychic body, and this intelligence is our personal Master.

Not deities. They are intelligences who were once mortals. They were on earth at one time, and successfully mastered their lives. They became Masters by learning how to awaken and apply the powers of Self so that they could direct the affairs of their lives consonantly with Cosmic purposes. By such development, they rose to that soul-personality development where it became no longer necessary for them to incarnate in physical form. One cannot expect that a Cosmic Master will be literally assigned to him as a personal servant and guide combined! Until we have prepared ourselves, we are not worthy of the assistance the Cosmic Masters can give. A Visible Master is one who has attained some degree of perfection, or a high sense of mastership of laws and principles, but who lives in the flesh on this earth plane.

The theater of motion, in that the force which produces matter and is the essence of matter, is motion or the vibration of Spirit. Matter is constantly changing. It does not exist independent of the spirit energy of which it consists. Matter is essential to expression or existence on this earth plane and should not be negated. In the composition of matter there are three elements: the electron, the atom, and the molecule.

A trickster-culture-hero found, with local variations, across nearly all of Polynesia, credited with slowing the sun to lengthen the day, fishing up islands (including, in Maori tradition, New Zealand's North Island) from the sea floor, and bringing fire to humanity. A demigod whose exploits combine cleverness, transgression, and real cost, since his final, overreaching attempt to conquer death itself is what ends his story.

The life force or vital essence held to reside in every person, creature, and natural feature — forests, rivers, and stones no less than living beings — making the mauri of a place, not only of a person, something that can be depleted, protected, or restored.

The power by which the one, undivided Brahman appears as the manifold, changing world of separate forms and selves — commonly translated “illusion,” though more precisely a veiling: not that the world is unreal, but that its apparent separateness conceals a deeper unity.

A circle, often laid out in stone on the land itself, divided into four quarters aligned to the cardinal directions, each associated with a color, an element, a stage of life, and a teaching. Used across many Plains and other Native traditions for ceremony, teaching, and orientation, the medicine wheel maps the moving parts of a life or a year onto a single, whole, unbroken circle.

A transformation of consciousness. When we meditate we change our state of receptivity, like tuning to a higher wave length. Meditation is attunement. Concentration is the focus of consciousness. Contemplation is the interrelation of thought. Concentration is the focusing of the mind upon some precept or idea. Meditation is the passive process of the mind. In meditation we employ concentration to will ourselves to be sensitive only to impressions other than those of the objective sense faculties. We suppress the objective senses and force a passive state.

That function of mind which receives, conserves, and reproduces impressions. It begins with the first conscious thought of our first incarnation and continues through all incarnations to the present time. We call the perfect memory the complete storehouse of facts and experiences. It is located in the subconscious mind. In order to reach the storehouse of memory, it is necessary to make the objective mind dormant so the subconscious mind may rise in power.

The little world or miniature of the universe or Macrocosm. The words come from the Greek, Mikros, meaning small; Makros, meaning great; and Kosmos, meaning world. The vital movements of the Microcosm exactly correspond to those of the Macrocosm and from this is derived the expression, “As above, so below.” Man, the Microcosm, is a counterpart of the universe.

The spiritual aspect of ordinary reality itself—this same physical world, but perceived and traveled in the shamanic state of consciousness, where the spirits of places, plants, and living things may be met without leaving the here and now.

The mystic makes a distinction between brain and mind. The brain is a physical organ for some of the functioning of mind. Mind works through the brain to a great extent, but not exclusively. Mind is divided into two domains of functioning, subconscious and objective. The objective has associated with it a subjective aspect, as in memory and imagination. We may think of the whole of consciousness as being like a graduated scale of vibratory energy. At one end are those levels with which we are most familiar, the objective and subjective aspects. The subconscious is that level which lies behind our realization of self and of externality. The objective mind is the consciousness of externality, of the actuality existing beyond ourselves. The subjective mind is consciousness of vibrations having an immediate origin different from those of our objective senses, such as reason, will, imagination. The subconscious mind constitutes those functions of mind of which we have no consciousness in the same manner as we do objectively and subjectively.

The result, not of supernatural, but of natural law. They are miracles only to those who do not understand what is meant by natural law. A miracle is any occurrence which appears to be contrary to nature and for which no natural cause is evident.

Liberation from samsara, the cycle of death and rebirth driven by karma and ignorance of one's true nature — the recognition of Atman as Brahman, and the release from the illusion of separateness that recognition brings.

The intimate and direct awareness of God or the Cosmic through self, that is, through the domain of the subconscious. The ideal of mysticism is the ultimate attainment of conscious union with the absolute, or the Cosmic. Mysticism teaches Cosmic laws and principles by which man is brought into closer consciousness of his divine power. The mystical experience of union with the One imposes upon the mystic a moral obligation. He must utilize his knowledge for the welfare of other men. Mysticism is not mystery. Mystery is commonly related to magic, deception, and delusion. The mysteries of Egypt and the Orphic and Eleusinian Schools of Greece alluded to a secret gnosis or wisdom, not to be profaned by divulging it to the masses. To the ancients it was a sacred knowledge to command the spiritual response of the individual.

A Rosicrucian ceremony, performed in Rosicrucian temples, for the naming of children. The age of the child must not exceed eighteen months, and one or both parents must be members of the Order. Certain promises are exacted from the parents, such as pledging that the child will be properly educated during his youth in non-sectarian schools; that he will be given every opportunity to enter the Order at the proper age without interference or unnecessary urging.

That law or set of laws decreed in The Beginning by the Divine Mind as the working basis of all creation and without which no manifestation can occur and exist. It is universal in scope and manner of operation, simple and direct. Natural law is always constructive even when it seems indisputably destructive. It is the expression or manifestation of Cosmic energy and order which man is able to discern. There is no such thing as supernatural law. There is nothing more divine than nature, nothing super beyond the natural. The greatest of miracles are not the result of the application of some supernatural law, but of a natural law.

Nerves are long cords of tissue distributed through the physical body by means of which the parts of the body are supplied with nerve energy. The source of this energy is the vital life force. It is Cosmic energy like electrical energy which is of a high rate of vibration. The central location of the spinal nervous system is in the cerebrum, that of the sympathetic system in the cerebellum. The points of intercommunication are the two small glands in the head. Every part of man’s body has both spinal and sympathetic nerves connected to it. The sympathetic system belongs to and functions almost exclusively in the psychic body of man. The spinal system belongs to the physical part of man and functions almost exclusively in it. It is the sympathetic nervous system that sends to every part of the body the curative, creative energy that cures, repairs, and builds the body.

The first stage of the Magnum Opus—the complete dissolution and putrefaction of the prima materia, pictured as a death the old substance must undergo before anything new can be composed of it. Psychologically, the nigredo is the descent into darkness, confusion, and the confrontation with one's own unmanageability, without which no further transformation is possible.

Liberation from samsara: the “blowing out” of the fires of craving, aversion, and delusion that Buddhist teaching holds to be the root cause of suffering. Not, in the classical account, an afterlife destination or a place at all, but the cessation of the very conditions that produce rebirth and dissatisfaction.

The traditional Sami shaman: healer, diviner, and ritual intermediary for a siida (a Sami community), who entered trance — most often with the aid of the drum and joik — to journey across a cosmos of upper, middle, and lower worlds, retrieve lost souls, and negotiate with the spirits governing the hunt, weather, and health.
These concern the nature and function of Nous, and may be found in the Fourth Degree of the Rosicrucian teachings.

The realm entered through the shamanic journey: a parallel dimension, experienced as fully real, in which spirits, power animals, and the dead may be encountered, and in which the ordinary limits of time and space do not hold.

A universal cosmic creative force, a harmony of dual polarities of energy. It operates through a system of harmonics by means of a Cosmic Keyboard of eighty octaves. The positive aspect of Nous emanates as a vital life force which impregnates matter and makes it living and conscious. It is predominantly positive, but has a negative quality. The negative polarity of Nous is spirit, meaning literally energy. It also has a positive quality. The positive quality of Nous is infinite, indefinite, unlimited; the negative is finite, definite, limited. Nous is vibratory in character, binary in nature, triune in manifestation.

Just before one attains a quickening of the inner consciousness, a real psychic unfoldment, there is a period of great darkness for the soul. The ancient Essenes were the first to call this the Obscure Night of the Soul. During this period the individual is stripped of all his vanities, self-assurance, and pride in whatever achievement or talents he may have. He stands naked before his own inner vision, seeing his weaknesses and realizing himself as he is, and he does not like what he sees. It is a time of personal readjustment of one’s spiritual and mental selves, a reorganization of the whole being. It is the great crucible in which we are purged of our weaknesses in preparation for the Golden Dawn, the great initiation just ahead. The Golden Dawn is the New Birth into the Greater Light.

The chief god of the Norse pantheon: god of wisdom, war, poetry, and the dead, who traded one eye for a drink from the well of wisdom and won the runes only by hanging, pierced by his own spear, from the World Tree Yggdrasil for nine nights without food or water — knowledge, in his own myth, paid for at the price of the body.

The earliest known script of the Irish language, carved as sets of notched lines along a central stemline and traditionally attributed to the god Ogma. Each letter is also named for a tree, so ogham doubles as a system of tree lore used in divination as well as writing.

The primordial sound and most sacred syllable of Hinduism, said to be the vibration from which the universe itself was spoken into being.
